text:
Leon Draisaitl has been the best scorer in the league's first quarter by most measures: 46 points (22 goals) in 25 games, 18 on the power play, a 10-game point streak per CBS Sports, and the third-most wins added among 548 skaters by our count. He is doing it after Mike Babcock split him from Connor McDavid, a move The New York Times asked about as "a quick fix or a long-term need."

The underlying play is excellent. Edmonton takes 60% of the 5v5 shot attempts and 58.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, about 21 points better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season.

The pace is not all skill, though. He has 22 goals on 14.7 expected, shooting 23% against 19% last season, and the Oilers have scored 24.0 more goals than their chances deserved with him on. Finishing and on-ice luck like that rarely hold for a full season. Our range for his season is 122 to 153 points, which allows for both the talent and the regression.
